name: First-Time Lisbon Guide
description: 30 stops in geographic walking order across four days: Belem & Alcantara, Baixa-Chiado-Bairro Alto-Principe Real, Graca-Castelo-Alfama, and a Sintra hike.

stops.title: Mosteiro dos Jerónimos
stops.narrative: UNESCO-listed Manueline monastery commissioned by King Manuel I to celebrate Vasco da Gama's route to India. Closed Mondays — go early.

stops.title: Pastéis de Belém
stops.narrative: The original custard-tart bakery, baking to the same secret recipe since 1837, right by the monastery.

stops.title: Padrão dos Descobrimentos
stops.narrative: Monument to the Discoveries, a riverside sail-shaped tribute to Portugal's Age of Exploration.

stops.title: Belém Tower
stops.narrative: The iconic 16th-century riverside fortress guarding the Tagus, symbol of Portugal's maritime age. Closed Mondays.

stops.title: MAAT — Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
stops.narrative: Striking modern riverside museum built beside the old Central Tejo power station.

stops.title: LX Factory
stops.narrative: Converted 19th-century textile factory in Alcântara, now a hub of design shops, street art and cafés.

stops.title: Rio Maravilha
stops.narrative: Rooftop restaurant inside LX Factory with sunset views over the 25 de Abril bridge.

stops.title: Praça do Comércio
stops.narrative: Grand riverside square flanked by yellow arcaded buildings, Lisbon's ceremonial gateway from the water.

stops.title: Arco da Rua Augusta
stops.narrative: Triumphal arch marking the entrance to the pedestrianised Rua Augusta; climb it for a rooftop view over Baixa.

stops.title: Rossio
stops.narrative: Praça Dom Pedro IV — Lisbon's liveliest square, with wave-patterned cobblestones and the Rossio train station nearby.

stops.title: Elevador de Santa Justa
stops.narrative: Neo-Gothic 1901 lift connecting Baixa to the Carmo ruins above, with an observation deck over the rooftops.

stops.title: Carmo Convent
stops.narrative: Roofless earthquake-ruined convent church at the top of the Santa Justa lift, now an archaeology museum.

stops.title: Café A Brasileira
stops.narrative: Historic 1905 coffee house on Rua Garrett in Chiado, famous for its bronze statue of poet Fernando Pessoa outside.

stops.title: A Cevicheria
stops.narrative: Small, popular Peruvian-Portuguese ceviche bar near Príncipe Real — expect a short wait.

stops.title: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
stops.narrative: Bairro Alto's best-atmosphere viewpoint — tiled balustrades, a kiosk bar and one of the best sunsets in the city.

stops.title: Jardim França Borges
stops.narrative: Leafy square built around a century-old cedar tree, ringed by Lisbon's specialty coffee scene. The garden at the centre of Praça do Príncipe Real.

stops.title: Dramático
stops.narrative: Small, tightly-edited specialty coffee bar just off Príncipe Real, across from the botanical garden.

stops.title: Essencial
stops.narrative: Intimate Bairro Alto dinner spot serving a Portuguese tasting menu in a house-like setting.

stops.title: Incognito
stops.narrative: 30-year-old Lisbon institution for indie, synthpop and post-punk nights.

stops.title: Music Box
stops.narrative: Brick-arched club under the railway on Pink Street in Cais do Sodré, known for cutting-edge music bookings.

stops.title: Cervejaria Ramiro
stops.narrative: Legendary seafood cervejaria near Intendente — go early or expect a queue.

stops.title: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
stops.narrative: Lisbon's highest viewpoint — a full 270-degree panorama over the castle, river and bridge from Graça.

stops.title: National Pantheon
stops.narrative: Dramatic white-domed National Pantheon, a former church now housing the tombs of Portuguese notables. Closed Mondays.

stops.title: Lisbon Castle
stops.narrative: Hilltop Moorish castle with battlements to walk and the best wide view over the Baixa grid.

stops.title: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
stops.narrative: Classic azulejo-framed Alfama viewpoint over the rooftops to the river — best around sunrise.

stops.title: Cathedral of Lisbon
stops.narrative: The fortress-like Lisbon Cathedral, built in 1147 on the site of a former mosque.

stops.title: Museu do Fado
stops.narrative: Museum dedicated to fado, the melancholic musical tradition born in these Alfama alleys.

stops.title: Cantinho do Aziz
stops.narrative: Beloved family-run restaurant on the Alfama/Mouraria edge — book ahead for an evening with fado nearby.

stops.title: Lux Frágil
stops.narrative: Portugal's most internationally renowned club, on the river by Santa Apolónia — best after 2am.

stops.title: The Moorish Castle
stops.narrative: Half-day hike from Sintra train station up the Moorish castle ramparts and on through forest to Pena Palace, roughly 9-10km round trip.
